correctness.rationale: Every edge changes one ternary coordinate by one unit, giving the ambient \(\ell_1\) lower bound. If a target-only coordinate exists, or a common support coordinate keeps its sign, that coordinate anchors an ambient geodesic away from the deleted origin. If equal supports have all signs reversed and support size at least two, two supported coordinates can alternate as anchors. Only opposite unit vectors force every two-step ambient geodesic through the deleted origin; bipartiteness excludes distance three and an explicit four-edge detour exists. Removing origin-endpoint pairs from the full ternary-cube product enumerator and moving exactly \(2m\) ordered pairs from degree two to degree four gives the stated polynomial. Differentiation at one gives the Wiener index. The inspected BFS verifier exhausts dimensions \(m=2,3,4,5\) as a consistency check, not as the infinite proof.

final_claim: For coherent monotone paths on the oriented cross-polytope, flip distance is ambient ternary \(\ell_1\) distance except for opposite unit sign vectors, whose distance is four; hence the complete ordered distance enumerator is \((3+4z+2z^2)^m-2(1+2z)^m+1+2m(z^4-z^2)\) and the Wiener index is \(4m9^{m-1}-2m3^{m-1}+2m\).
